language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi, I'm Chip.
Hello, my name is Linda. Today I have come along with my dad to enjoy the beauty of nature.
My Dad is a ranger in a Wild Park in Africa. His job is to take care of  wild life.
Today we spotted some deer and African wild dogs in the park.
Some deer roam in groups while others go alone. The African wild dog hunts them in packs and small groups.
Oh look! There is one deer over there!
See….One more deer has just joined her. You can use Math to calculate how many there are now, like this:
There are 2 deer now! Can you help me today?

I am counting deer. Can you help me choose the right calculation? Remember, when more deer are added to a group you use the + symbol. If you take deer away from a group you use the – symbol.

helperSimple.text: Help Linda count the deer in each group!

activities.title:
There are two deer standing by the tree.
They are joined by two other deer.
Which calculation should we use?

There are three African wild dogs standing in the park.
They are joined by another African wild dog.
Which calculation should we use?

There are six African wild dogs standing in the park.
Three African wild dogs leave the group.
Which calculation should we use?

There are five deer standing by the tree.
Two deer leave the group.
Which calculation should we use?

There are five deer standing by the tree.
They are joined by three other deer.
Which calculation should we use?

outro.text: Thank you! My father will be very happy that we have completed the counting of groups!
